pr_body:
Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/35613

`time` is still logged to the second, but it's passed thru to `W3CLogger` with millisecond precision so we can more accurately calculate `time-taken`. Logs for the sample now generally have `time-taken` at under 1 millisecond, rather than how many milliseconds past the second the action occurred at.
pr_comments: Updated for feedback. Time-taken is now calculated entirely in the middleware using `ValueStopWatch`. Added/changed tests to reflect that.

issue_context.title: W3CLogging "time" not precise enough, leading to "time-taken" being significantly wrong

### Describe the bug
When using the new W3CLogging, I've noticed that the "time" field is only precise down to the second.  This does not match many other web servers, including IIS, which log times with millisecond precision. Also, the "time-taken" field is calculated based on this imprecision "time" value, thus leading to very inaccurate time-taken values in the logs.  For example, if a request comes in at 01:30:00.800 and takes 10 milliseconds to process, then the time-taken that is written to the logs is 810 milliseconds, not the expected 10 milliseconds

### To Reproduce
<!--
We ❤ code! Point us to a minimalistic repro project hosted in a GitHub repo.
For a repro project, create a new ASP.NET Core project using the template of your your choice, apply the minimum required code to result in the issue you're observing.

We will close this issue if:
- the repro project you share with us is complex. We can't investigate custom projects, so don't point us to such, please.
- if we will not be able to repro the behavior you're reporting
-->

1. In VS 2022, create a new ASP.NET Core Web App, targetting .NET 6.0 (Preview)
2. In the Program.cs file, add the following immediately before `var app = builder.Build();`

`builder.Services.AddW3CLogging(logging =>
{
    logging.LoggingFields = Microsoft.AspNetCore.HttpLogging.W3CLoggingFields.All;
});`

Also add the following immediately after `var app = builder.Build();`

`app.UseW3CLogging();`

3. Run the application, refresh the page several times, and take a look at the resulting w3clog-*.txt file.   You'll note that the "time" column is formatted as hh:mm:ss, but no milliseconds, and that the time-taken is all over the place, even though we are hitting a very simple page that in actuality is taking under 100ms to process.

### Exceptions (if any)
<!-- 
Include the exception you get when facing this issue
-->

No exception, just inaccurate time-taken values

comments:
This is the related code in the W3CLogger that I believe is causing the time-taken to not be accurate:

https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/3c089fa29a441a390f2786e5107f0dcc8397898f/src/Middleware/HttpLogging/src/W3CLogger.cs#L51-L59

I believe simply adding the milliseconds to the time field and parsing it with the milliseconds included when calculating the time-taken would fix this issue.

I'm surprised that IIS logs to millisecond precision, the w3c spec calls for both `time` and `time-taken` to use second precision: https://www.w3.org/TR/WD-logfile.html. I agree that millisecond precision would be more informative here, so if the choice is between following the spec and matching IIS, I'm inclined to think that the usefulness of millisecond precision would break the tie here in favor of matching IIS. @Tratcher do you agree?
Agreed, use milliseconds. Most requests should not take a full second so that's not a useful unit anymore.
Should be a quick fix, I'll include it for RC2.

review_comments:
Is the fractional part needed?
```suggestion
                shouldLog |= AddToList(elements, _timeTakenIndex, stopWatch.GetElapsedTime().TotalMilliseconds.ToString("F0", CultureInfo.InvariantCulture));
```
Many request/response pairs take <1 ms, so I like having the precision. Our Console Logger also logs fractional milliseconds.
